standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space commutes with filtered colimits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-colimits (invoked at proof line 726)
standard_prerequisites.use: It settles the remaining statement for the quasi-compact quasi-separated space $X \times_Y V$.

core_obligations: Identify the morphism of topoi $f_{small}$ with the morphism of sites given by $V \mapsto X \times_Y V$ on the small etale sites (proof lines 712-717).

Apply the general colimit criterion for a morphism of sites, and use that every object of $Y_{spaces,\acute{e}tale}$ is covered by affine objects to reduce to: for $V$ affine and etale over $Y$, the cohomology $H^p(X \times_Y V, \mathcal{F})$ is the filtered colimit of the $H^p(X \times_Y V, \mathcal{F}_i)$ (proof lines 718-723).

Observe that $X \times_Y V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because $V$ is affine and $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and conclude with the colimit statement for that space (proof lines 724-727).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to affine objects of the target site (proof lines 718-723).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the higher direct images of a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces commute with filtered colimits of abelian sheaves (statement lines 696-709, with the slogan recording this reading). The proof passes to the morphism of small etale sites determined by the fibre product functor, invokes the general criterion for colimits along a morphism of sites, and reduces to an affine object of the target, where the fibre product is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and the known colimit statement applies. The reduction to the affine members of a covering is the substance, so the claim is H2.
